title: Localization dimension for finite type domain
statement: For a field k and a finite type k-algebra domain S, every maximal ideal m of S satisfies ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime m) = ringKrullDim S.

proof.text: Apply the existing common maximal-chain length theorem to obtain a natural number d, dim S = d, and length d for every maximal prime LTSeries. In particular the spectrum is finite-dimensional.

For the given maximal ideal m, Mathlib Ideal.exists_ltSeries_length_eq_height gives a prime LTSeries c ending at m with length equal to height(m). The height of c at each index is that index. Hence its head is minimal and adjacent terms cover one another: an intervening prime would force two height increments between consecutive indices. Its last term is maximal because m is maximal. A finite saturated chain with minimal head and maximal last term is a maximal chain: any extra comparable element must lie below every term, above every term, or strictly between adjacent terms, all impossible. Both order-theoretic arguments are fully proved as local facts within the target theorem; no helper declaration is added.
Apply the common-chain-length theorem to c. Its length is d, so height(m) = d = dim S. This includes d = 0, when the chain has one term and no covering conditions.
Use IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height to rewrite the dimension of S_m as height(m), and conclude dim S_m = dim S.

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OS, final inference from the common maximal-chain length; reuse the sibling chains declaration and prove the finite-order glue in Lean. Official source consulted at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OS.
